states.standardNote: Retail rates count only if not unreasonable, and wage rates paid by similar dealers in the state are a factor.
states.labor: Total labor charges on qualified ROs divided by hours, from fewer of 100 sequential or 90 days, last 180 days.
states.parts: Total parts charges divided by parts cost, minus 1, times 100. Same ROs or a separate set.
states.response: Effective 45 days after OEM receives it unless OEM rebuts once in that window. Court win is retroactive to day 45.

states.standardNote: The manufacturer can disapprove a rate that is materially miscalculated or unreasonable compared to similar dealers in Alaska.
states.labor: Not less than the dealer's rate for similar retail nonwarranty work, unless otherwise agreed. No RO method for labor.
states.parts: Lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 90 days of ROs, from the last 180 days.
states.response: Disapprove within 30 days or deemed approved. Takes effect no more than 30 days after approval.

states.standardNote: The manufacturer can rebut within 30 days if the rate is inaccurate or unreasonable compared to similar same-make dealers in Arizona.
states.labor: Optional RO method: lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 90 days, from the last 180 days. Labor sales divided by hours.
states.parts: Same RO sample as labor. Parts sales divided by parts cost, minus 1, as a percentage.
states.response: Rebut within 30 days and propose an adjustment, otherwise effective 30 days after the manufacturer receives the declaration.

states.standardNote: The retail rate applies only if it is reasonable compared to same-make dealers in the dealer's market area.
states.labor: Retail labor rate: labor sales divided by hours on qualified customer-pay ROs, lesser of 100 sequential or 90 days, last 180 days.
states.parts: Retail markup from the same qualified ROs: parts sales divided by cost, minus 1, as a percentage.
states.response: Approve or disapprove a rate change request within 45 days, or it is deemed approved. Effective date not stated.

states.labor: Total labor charges on the submitted ROs divided by the hours that produced them.
states.parts: Total parts charges divided by parts cost, minus 1, times 100. Same ROs or a separate set.
states.response: OEM may contest within 30 days, only for material inaccuracy or fraud. Uncontested rate takes effect day 30 after receipt.

states.labor: Dealer's choice: 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or all customer-pay ROs over 90 days, from the last 90 days. Sales divided by hours.
states.parts: Same RO options, separately or together with labor. Parts sales divided by cost, minus 1, as a percentage.
states.frequency: Once a year for labor and once a year for parts
states.response: Contest within 45 days only if materially inaccurate, otherwise effective day 45. Rate set in a dispute applies back to day 30.

states.standardNote: The manufacturer can rebut within 30 days by showing the rate is unfair compared to same-make dealers in the vicinity.
states.labor: All customer-pay ROs from the month before submission. Total labor sales divided by labor hours.
states.parts: Lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 60 days of ROs, from the last 180 days.
states.response: Rebut within 30 days and propose an adjustment within 30 days, otherwise effective 30 days after declaration, subject to audit.

states.labor: Rate from the lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 90 days of ROs, from the last 180 days.
states.parts: Markup from the same RO sample.
states.response: Effective within 30 days of submission and presumed fair. A manufacturer info request within 30 days restarts the clock.

states.labor: If no agreement in 30 days, dealer picks greater of prior month's retail labor sales divided by hours, or gross profit method.
states.parts: If no agreement in 30 days, greater of markup on 50 consecutive retail ROs in 3 months, OEM list price, or gross profit method.
states.frequency: Twice a year at most (parts or labor)
states.response: Any increase is paid retroactively on claims filed from 15 days after the OEM receives the request.

states.standardNote: The manufacturer can contest the rate by showing it is unreasonable compared with similarly situated dealers nearby.
states.labor: Labor sales divided by hours, from the lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 90 days of ROs, last 180 days.
states.parts: Markup from the same kind of RO sample: parts sales divided by cost, minus 1, times 100.
states.response: Approve or disapprove within 30 days, or deemed approved. Effective 30 days after approval.

states.standardNote: Labor must be paid at the retail rate, but the parts markup must not be unreasonable compared to same-make dealers in Hawaii.
states.labor: Not less than, and not more than, the dealer's retail labor rate. No RO method for labor.
states.parts: 100 qualifying consecutive customer-pay ROs from recent months. If unavailable, all ROs of all types from the prior 2 months.
states.response: Parts markup takes effect within 90 days of submission. Requests for more information restart the clock.

states.standardNote: The retail rate must not be unreasonable compared to same or competing franchises in the dealer's area.
states.labor: Same RO sample as parts: lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 90 days, from the last 180 days.
states.parts: Lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 90 days, from the last 180 days. Menu-priced work excluded.
states.response: Effective within 90 days of submission. Manufacturer may request more information within 30 days, which restarts the clock.

states.standardNote: The parts retail price must not be unreasonable compared with same-make dealers in the area, and the OEM may audit the parts sample.
states.labor: Effective labor rate from 100 sequential customer-pay ROs chosen by the dealer, minus simple maintenance ROs.
states.parts: Lesser of 100 sequential or 90 days of customer-pay ROs, from the last 180 days; declare average markup.
states.frequency: Labor once a calendar year; parts twice a calendar year
states.response: Parts markup effective 30 days after declaration, subject to OEM audit within 30 days. Labor: not stated in the statute.

states.labor: Labor sales divided by hours in 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 90 days of ROs, from the last 180 days.
states.parts: Lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 90 days. Parts charges divided by cost, minus 1. Last 180 days.
states.response: Rebut within 60 days if unreasonable or materially inaccurate, otherwise effective automatically.

states.standardNote: The retail rate applies only if reasonable, and the manufacturer can deny it but must prove the denial was reasonable.
states.labor: Lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 90 days, from the last 180 days. Labor sales divided by hours.
states.parts: Same RO sample. Parts charges divided by cost, minus 1, as a percentage.
states.response: May audit within 30 days, then approve or deny. Effective 45 days after approval.

states.standardNote: The retail rate applies only if reasonable, and the manufacturer can deny it but must prove the denial was reasonable.
states.labor: Lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 90 days, from the last 180 days. Labor sales divided by hours.
states.parts: Same RO sample. Parts charges divided by cost, minus 1, as a percentage.
states.response: May audit within 30 days, then approve or deny. Effective 45 days after approval.

states.standardNote: No RO sample method. The statute sets a floor at the dealer's retail charges, with parts at least cost plus 30%.
states.labor: No less than the dealer's charge to retail customers for like nonwarranty service. No RO sample method.
states.parts: No less than the dealer's retail charge, with a minimum of dealer cost plus 30% gross profit.
states.response: Not stated in the statute

states.labor: Total labor charges divided by hours, from the fewer of 100 sequential qualifying ROs or 90 days of ROs, last 180 days.
states.parts: Markup from the same RO sample: total parts charges divided by parts cost, minus 1, times 100.
states.response: Presumed accurate. Effective 45 days after receipt unless the manufacturer rebuts within 45 days.

states.labor: The dealer's retail labor rate, as long as it is posted where service customers can see it. No RO method.
states.parts: Average markup from the lesser (by total cost) of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 60 days of ROs, last 180 days.
states.frequency: Twice a year (parts markup, per calendar year). Not stated for labor.
states.response: Parts markup takes effect 30 days after the declaration, subject to manufacturer audit and adjustment.

states.labor: Retail labor rate from whichever gives fewer ROs: 100 sequential qualifying customer-pay ROs or 90 days, within the last 180 days.
states.parts: Cost plus retail markup from the same RO sample: total parts charges divided by total parts cost, minus 1.
states.response: Approve or rebut within 30 days; if no rebuttal, effective day 31. If approved, payment starts within 30 days.

states.labor: Lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 60 consecutive days, last 180 days. Total labor sales divided by labor hours.
states.parts: Average markup from the same RO method, unless dealer and manufacturer agree in writing on a markup within 30 days of request.
states.frequency: Once a year (per calendar year, parts and labor)
states.response: Effective day 30 after declaration, subject to audit. Manufacturer must propose any adjustment within 30 days of submission.

states.standardNote: The manufacturer can contest using the parts prices and labor rates of similar same-make dealers in a comparable area of Michigan.
states.labor: Total labor sales divided by hours, from lesser of 100 consecutive customer-pay ROs or 90 days, last 180 days.
states.parts: Total parts sales divided by parts cost, minus 1, times 100, from the same RO sample.
states.response: OEM approves or disapproves within 45 days, or it is deemed approved. Effective 30 days after approval.

states.standardNote: The manufacturer can disapprove using comparable same-make dealers' rates in a comparable area of the state.
states.labor: At dealer's election: total customer labor charges divided by labor hours, from the parts RO sample, times the dealer's time guide.
states.parts: At dealer's election: lesser of 100 sequential or 90 days of customer-pay ROs with warranty-like repairs, last 180 days. Otherwise cost plus reasonable markup.
states.response: Disapprove in writing within 30 days with substantiation and a proposed adjustment, or the rate is approved. Effective date not stated.

states.labor: Rate from the fewer of 100 sequential qualifying ROs or 90 days of ROs, from the last 180 days.
states.parts: Markup from the same RO sample.
states.response: Effective 45 days after submission unless the manufacturer rebuts within 45 days.

states.standardNote: Retail rates are the principal factor for reasonable compensation, not a fixed formula, and there is no RO-sample method.
states.labor: No less than the dealer's posted nonwarranty labor rate (§407.583). Retail labor rates are the principal factor.
states.parts: The amount the dealer charges retail customers for similar parts is the primary factor. No RO method.
states.frequency: Twice a year (labor or parts rate requests, per calendar year)
states.response: Not stated in the statute. A denied rate increase can be appealed to the Administrative Hearing Commission within 60 days.

states.labor: Fewer ROs of 100 sequential qualified ROs or 90 consecutive days, last 180 days. Total labor charges divided by hours charged.
states.parts: Same RO method: total parts charges divided by total parts cost, minus 1, times 100.
states.frequency: Once per 12 months (labor and parts each)
states.response: Effective day 30 after receipt unless manufacturer objects within 30 days that the rate is materially inaccurate.

states.standardNote: The RO sample method covers parts only. Labor must be no less than the dealer's retail or fleet rate, with local dealer wage rates as a principal factor.
states.labor: No less than the dealer's rate to retail or fleet customers. Prevailing local dealer wage rates are a principal factor.
states.parts: Average markup from the lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 90 days of ROs, from the last 180 days.
states.response: Manufacturer may audit and approve or deny within 30 days. Markup takes effect 45 days after approval.

states.labor: No less than what the dealer charges retail customers for nonwarranty labor. No RO method.
states.parts: No less than what the dealer charges retail customers for parts. No RO method.
states.response: Not stated in the statute

states.standardNote: The declared parts rate must be reasonable compared with similar-size same-make dealers nearby.
states.labor: No less than what the dealer charges retail customers for like nonwarranty work. No RO method for labor.
states.parts: If no agreed markup within 30 days: lesser of 100 sequential or 90 consecutive days of customer-pay ROs, last 180 days.
states.response: Effective day 30 after submission. Manufacturer must signal rebuttal by day 30 and propose an adjustment by day 60.

states.labor: Average hourly rate from the lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 90 days of ROs, from the last 180 days.
states.parts: Average parts markup from the lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 90 days of ROs, from the last 180 days.
states.response: Effective 30 days after the dealer's declaration. The manufacturer may adjust only through an audit of the submitted sample.

states.citation: N.M. Stat. Ann. §57-16-7 (as amended by Laws 2018, ch. 28, SB 27)
states.standardNote: The manufacturer can refuse an increase if the rate was miscalculated or unreasonably exceeds all other same or competing line dealers in the market area.
states.labor: Lesser of 100 sequential or 90 days of customer-pay ROs, last 180 days, declaring the average customer-pay labor rate.
states.parts: Cost plus average markup from the lesser of 100 sequential or 90 days of customer-pay ROs, last 180 days.
states.frequency: Twice a year (per calendar year, parts and labor)
states.response: Parts markup takes effect 30 days after submission. Not stated for labor.

states.standardNote: The manufacturer can rebut by showing the rate is unreasonable compared with all same-make dealers in the vicinity.
states.labor: Not less than the dealer's rate to non-warranty customers for like service. No RO method stated for labor.
states.parts: Lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 90 days of ROs, from the last 180 days; declare average markup.
states.response: Declared rate takes effect 30 days after declaration. If rebutted, dealer can resubmit within 60 days; OEM responds within 60 days.

states.labor: Average labor rate from lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 60 days with warranty-like parts, last 180 days.
states.parts: Average markup from the same RO sample (lesser of 100 sequential or 60 days, last 180 days).
states.response: OEM may rebut within 30 days as inaccurate, proposing an adjustment by day 60. If dealer wins a protest, effective day 60.

states.labor: Same RO sample as parts. Total labor sales divided by hours, times the dealer's own time guide.
states.parts: Average markup from the lesser of 100 sequential or 90 consecutive days of customer-pay ROs with warranty-like parts, last 180 days.
states.frequency: Once per 12 months (parts and labor each)
states.response: Contest within 30 days with calculations and a proposed rate, or approved. Effective day 30 after receipt.

states.labor: Total labor sales divided by labor hours, from 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or all ROs in 90 days, last 180 days.
states.parts: Total parts sales divided by parts cost, minus 1, times 100. Same ROs or a separate set.
states.response: OEM may contest within 30 days as materially inaccurate; otherwise rate takes effect. Disputed outcome applies retroactively from day 30.

states.labor: Labor sales divided by labor hours on the lesser of 100 sequential ROs or 90 days, last 180 days.
states.parts: Average markup on the same RO sample. One request can set parts, labor, or both.
states.response: Rebut within 45 days; rate takes effect 30 days after approval. Dealer may protest to the Commission.

states.standardNote: The manufacturer can contest using rates from at least 3 same-make dealers in contiguous or economically similar markets.
states.labor: Hourly rate from the lesser of 100 sequential ROs or 90 days, last 180 days. Never below the nonwarranty rate.
states.parts: Same RO sample. Pays what the dealer charges nonwarranty customers, if not unreasonable.
states.response: Contest within 30 days or it is approved; effective 30 days after approval.

states.standardNote: The manufacturer can rebut within 60 days by showing the declared rate is unreasonable or materially inaccurate.
states.labor: Total labor sales divided by labor hours, from lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 90 days, last 180 days.
states.parts: Average markup from lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 90 days with warranty-like parts, last 180 days.
states.response: OEM may rebut within 60 days. Otherwise the rate takes effect 60 days after the declaration.

states.citation: R.I. Gen. Laws §31-5.1-6, as amended by 2026 S 2347 / H 8213 (effective 10/1/2026)
states.standardNote: The manufacturer can rebut using rates at other same-make dealers nearby (for parts, their advertised retail rates in the relevant market area).
states.labor: Rate is labor sales over hours on all customer-pay ROs from the prior month, paid on technicians' actual punched time.
states.parts: Lesser of 100 sequential ROs or 60 days, last 180 days. Average markup on warranty-like parts.
states.response: Rebut within 30 days; rate takes effect 30 days after declaration. Dealer may protest to the department.

states.labor: Labor sales divided by hours on the lesser of 100 sequential ROs or 90 days, last 180 days.
states.parts: Same RO sample. Warranty parts paid at cost times 1 plus average markup.
states.response: Approve or deny (base deadline not stated; extended 30 days if more documents requested). Effective 30 days after approval.

states.labor: Not less than the dealer's nonwarranty labor rate. The manufacturer must rely on the dealer's written rate schedule.
states.parts: Not less than the dealer's current retail price for the parts.
states.response: Not stated in the statute

states.standardNote: Labor is set by the dealer's sworn rate statement to the Motor Vehicle Commission, not an RO sample. The RO method covers parts only.
states.labor: Dealer files a sworn retail labor rate with the commission. The manufacturer pays it unless it shows the commission the rate is improper.
states.parts: Markup from the lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or 90 days of ROs, from the last 180 days.
states.response: Parts: manufacturer approves or denies within 30 days. Effective 45 days after approval.

states.labor: Greater of average labor rate on 100 sequential non-warranty ROs or 90 consecutive days, both within prior 6 months.
states.parts: No markup method. General rule only: not less than what retail customers pay for similar work.
states.frequency: Once a year (labor), unless both sides agree
states.response: OEM approves or disapproves within 60 days. If the board sides with the dealer, rate is effective day 60.

states.labor: Labor charges divided by hours on qualified repairs: fewer of 100 sequential ROs or 90 days, last 180 days.
states.parts: Same RO sample. Parts charges divided by parts cost, minus 1, as a percentage.
states.frequency: Once per 12 months (labor and parts each)
states.response: Effective day 30 unless the manufacturer objects to accuracy or requests more ROs within 30 days. Payment starts within 15 days.

states.standardNote: The manufacturer can rebut using the practices of at least 4 nearby dealers of the same or a competing make.
states.labor: Dealer's retail labor rate, if routinely posted where service customers can see it.
states.parts: Lesser total cost of 100 sequential ROs or 60 days, last 180 days. Average markup.
states.response: Parts markup takes effect 30 days after declaration, subject to audit and adjustment.

states.labor: Not less than the retail rate. Increases based on 100 consecutive ROs or 90 days, whichever comes first.
states.parts: Agreed markup. If no agreement, average retail markup from the same RO sample.
states.response: Not stated in the statute

states.standardNote: The manufacturer can refuse a labor increase that unreasonably exceeds all same-market dealers' rates.
states.labor: Dealer's retail labor and diagnostic rate. No RO method stated. Dealer may resubmit if refused.
states.parts: Lesser of 100 sequential ROs or 90 days, last 180 days. Average markup.
states.response: Parts markup takes effect 30 days after submission. Labor response not stated.

states.standardNote: The manufacturer can rebut a rate as unreasonable compared with same-make dealers in an economically similar area of the state.
states.labor: Labor sales divided by hours on 100 sequential ROs or 90 days, last 180 days.
states.parts: Same RO sample or a separate one. Average markup on warranty-like parts.
states.frequency: Once per 12 months (parts and labor each)
states.response: Approve or rebut within 30 days or it is deemed approved; effective 30 days after approval.

states.standardNote: For parts, the manufacturer has a defense if the markup is not reasonably competitive with similar dealers in the state.
states.labor: Customer labor charges divided by the manufacturer's warranty time allowances for those repairs, from the RO sample.
states.parts: Lesser of 100 sequential ROs or 90 days, last 180 days. Cost times average markup.
states.response: Must start paying the substantiated rate within 30 days. May dispute in writing with an explanation.

states.labor: Labor charges divided by hours, from the lesser of 100 sequential qualified ROs or 90 days of ROs, last 180 days.
states.parts: Markup from the same RO sample.
states.frequency: Once per 12 months, unless set by mutual agreement
states.response: Manufacturer may request more ROs or contest within 30 days. Otherwise effective 45 days after receipt. Contests go to mediation.
